header.title: Curse tablets from Pannonia superior, in Greek (Epigraphic Database Heidelberg): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Greek curse tablets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:defix:edh:pannonia-superior-grc:grc, from the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.35450.1.1: A charm against migraine (ἡμικράνιον); Antaura is the migraine personified. 'Where are you taking the migraine' may instead mean 'where are you going? Into the head'. Artemis' reply (line 13) and the second side (line 14) are broken.
